quote: Welche im Variabelngrad höchste Ueberschiebung kann für eine Form nten Grades noch verschwinden und wie viel Parameter treten dann noch auf?
english: Which transvectant, highest in the degree of the variables, can still vanish for a form of degree n, and how many parameters then still occur?
topic: A list of research notes: treating certain functions by analogy with Eisenstein's work on the p-function via infinite products, addition theorems for p and σ, turning covariant criteria into invariant ones, decomposition conditions for binary forms in several variables, vanishing of transvectants, Klein's topic of a typical representation of the Kummer surface, and termination of chains of transvection processes.

triage.modern_statement: Let f be a binary form of degree n and consider its even transvectants with itself, (f,f)_{2k}, which are covariants of order 2n-4k. The question asks for the largest order in x (that is, the smallest k ≥ 1) for which (f,f)_{2k} can vanish identically for a nonzero f, ideally without f degenerating. It also asks for the dimension of the set of such f, meaning how many free parameters remain. A broader modern reading: describe the loci of binary forms on which a given transvectant (f,f)_{2k}, or more generally a given covariant, vanishes identically, and find their dimensions.
triage.answered_by: Only partial answers were found. The first case is classical: (f,f)_2 is, up to a constant, the Hessian, and it vanishes identically exactly when f is the n-th power of a linear form, which leaves 2 parameters (1 projectively). Hilbert's own later work built a covariant that vanishes exactly on the forms that are μ-th powers. For quartics, (f,f)_4 = 0 is a known special condition, the tetrahedral (equianharmonic) case. Modern papers on transvectants exist, e.g. Abdesselam & Chipalkatti, Ann. Inst. Fourier 2009, but I found no source that answers Hilbert's general question for arbitrary n and k.

evidence.claim: (f,f)_2 equals the Hessian up to a constant, and it vanishes if and only if f is a power of a linear form (shown for cubics, Prop. 2.7.2).
For binary forms, Hilbert built a covariant that vanishes exactly on the variety of μ-th powers. A degree-4 form vanishes on the vertices of a regular tetrahedron if and only if (f,f)_4 = 0.
Modern work on transvectants of binary forms: Abdesselam & Chipalkatti show the higher transvectants are redundant (Ann. Inst. Fourier 59(5), 2009, 1671-1713).
Hilbert covariants, which vanish on loci of forms with special root structure, are studied in modern algebraic geometry and described as covering much unexplored ground.

triage.why: This is a real but small research question in classical invariant theory about when a self-transvectant of a binary form vanishes identically. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. The sources confirm the Hessian case (f must be a perfect power of a linear form) and the special quartic case (f,f)_4 = 0. Modern work on Hilbert covariants and transvectants touches related loci. I could not find a source that answers the general question for all n and k or counts the parameters, and my search budget ran out before I could check further (for example, papers on loci of forms with vanishing transvectants). So the verdict is left as possibly unexplored, with low confidence.
